rootCause.mechanism: scripts/build.mjs treats every child stderr line (plus WARN/deprecated stdout lines) as a warning, accepts only exact allowlist signatures that are not expired and allowed for the release channel, then fails with 'Build emitted unregistered or expired warnings:' and exit 1
rootCause.observedFailure: The production build emitted rolldown [PLUGIN_TIMINGS] diagnostics (stderr) that are not in the allowlist → unexpectedWarnings → exit 1. The plugin-timings diagnostic is cache/speed-dependent: the warm-cache preview build did not emit it and passed.
rootCause.latentHazard: The single allowlist entry WARN-NITRO-001 ('inlineDynamicImports option is ignored…') has expiresOn 2026-10-06 and recheckedAt 2026-09-07 — already expired today (2026-10-12); if that warning reappears in any build, it fails as 'expired'. The expiry pattern is deliberate and documented (docs/runbooks/cutover-A4.md line 491; docs/specs/M-02/emenda-2026-09-07-env-guard.md line 129): expired = fail-closed.
rootCause.releaseChannel: releaseChannel = BUILD_RELEASE_CHANNEL ?? (CI ? 'unclassified-ci' : 'local'); the allowlist entry only covers [local, pre-beta-internal]

stateAfterFailure.newProductionDeployment: ERROR, unaliased (left in history as audit trail)

conclusion: Publishing the merged revision is blocked by the repository's own build-warning gate (fail-closed by design), not by the code or by Vercel. Fix requires re-checking the WARN-NITRO-001 entry (and deciding the PLUGIN_TIMINGS classification) through the develop circuit; retrying the same build may pass by cache luck but does not remove the blocker.
